source.document: IPU Pharmacist Assessment Form – Cold Sores
source.notes: Criteria are summarised for the prototype. The HSE CCS protocol remains the clinical reference.

tiers.label: Emergency referral to a hospital emergency department or emergency services

criteria.label: Systemically very unwell, or showing symptoms of severe or life-threatening infection or sepsis
criteria.note: Refer urgently to the emergency department by ambulance.

tiers.label: Urgent medical assessment (treating service, GP, GP out of hours or emergency department)

criteria.label: Under 1 month of age (corrected age for infants born pre-term)
Moderate to severe immunocompromise due to underlying medical conditions or treatments

tiers.label: Referral to a GP or other relevant practitioner – pharmacist prescribing not permitted

criteria.label: Contraindications as specified in the medicine's Summary of Product Characteristics
Pregnancy or suspected pregnancy (refer to GP or treating obstetrician/gynaecologist)
Symptoms not improving within 14 days, with or without treatment
Signs of secondary infection, e.g. very painful or very swollen
Suspected gingivostomatitis
criteria.note: May be referred to a dental practitioner.

criteria.label: Known hypersensitivity or adverse reaction to the treatment options or any of their components

tiers.label: Referral to a GP or other relevant practitioner – initial limited supply permitted

criteria.label: Immunocompromised due to underlying medical conditions or treatments (excluding moderate to severe immunocompromise)
Recurrent problematic lesions or frequently recurring infection

groups.label: Signs and symptoms typical of cold sores

items.label: Prodromal phase – tingling, itching or burning feeling on the lip
Fluid-filled blisters that may weep and crust over into a scab
Clusters of blisters or sores inside the mouth

groups.label: Other symptoms that may occur in children

typicalQuestion.label: Are symptoms typical of cold sores?

pathways.label: Meets the inclusion criteria – proceed with pharmacist prescribing and give advice and counselling

declaration.followUp: if my symptoms get worse or persist for longer than 14 days, with or without treatment

notes: See the HSE protocol and the Summary of Product Characteristics for dosage and notes for each medicine.

options.name: Aciclovir 5% w/w cream
options.dosage: Apply five times daily at approximately four-hourly intervals, omitting the night-time application, for at least 4 days. If healing has not occurred, continue for up to 10 days.
